key_insight: Sharing coefficients can be turned from a billing/allocation tool into day-ahead price signals that steer household demand toward local PV availability and reduce feeder reverse power flow.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical control layer for renewable energy communities because it couples market-like incentives with low-voltage network constraints.
method: Iteratively compute proportional PV sharing from household demand and PV forecasts.
Convert allocation results into feeder-aware or community-wide household price signals.
Use convex optimization to reshape loads and AC power flow analysis to assess network impact.
evidence_signal: Using measured profiles from 15 households, the method reduced feeder reverse energy by 45.0% and 44.6% on selected days, and by 69.0% and 66.3% over the annual window for feeder-aware and feeder-agnostic cases.
watch_item: Performance depends on forecast quality, household participation, and the added communication/optimization overhead needed to update price signals day ahead.
paper_title: Sharing Coefficient-Based Price Signals for Demand Response in Renewable Energy Communities
